description.content: Query measure values for counties, each with an explicit `value_state`.

Query published county observations for one measure and up to 500 counties.

### What it returns
Observations from the current release, ordered by measure ID, county FIPS, period start, then observation ID. You cannot sort or aggregate. Each observation carries its `value_state`, source, methodology, and limitations.

### Required parameters
Send `measure_id`, `geography_type=county`, one or more `geography_id` values, and the time parameter that the measure type accepts.

### Time parameters by measure type
| Measure type | Send | Wrong choice returns |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Annual surveillance (data is for 2023) | `year`, or `start_date` and `end_date` | 400 `INVALID_REQUEST` if you send both `year` and dates, or neither. 400 `UNSUPPORTED_FILTER` if you send `vintage_year`. |
| Daily environmental (January 2025 weather measures, enabled separately) | `start_date` and `end_date`, or `year` | 400 `INVALID_REQUEST` if you send only one date, or both `year` and dates. 400 `UNSUPPORTED_FILTER` if you send `vintage_year`. |
| CDC cumulative status (`scapularis_status`, `burgdorferi_status`) | `start_date=2025-12-31` and `end_date=2025-12-31` (grain `CUMULATIVE`) | 400 `UNSUPPORTED_FILTER` for `year` or any other date range. The API rejects it before it reads data. |
| County context vintages (SVI, population, insurance) | `vintage_year=2022` (periods are ACS 2018-2022) | 400 `INVALID_REQUEST` if `vintage_year` is missing. 400 `UNSUPPORTED_FILTER` for another vintage, `year`, `start_date`, or `end_date`. |
| RUCC (`rucc_2023`) | `vintage_year=2023` (categorical codes and labels, with `null` period dates) | 400 `INVALID_REQUEST` if `vintage_year` is missing. 400 `UNSUPPORTED_FILTER` for another vintage, `year`, `start_date`, or `end_date`. |

### Value states
| Case | How to read it |
| --- | --- |
| Environmental measures | Descriptive weather with labeled daily periods and `environmental_context` coverage. They have no strata and make no causal, disease-risk, or machine-learning claim. |
| Surveillance context | Optional, and it needs a published delivery. `normalized_state` preserves the publisher's meaning, and the publisher's value stays in `value`. |
| Missing context | It does not establish absence or temporal comparability. |
| Absent county context rows | They are unavailable evidence, never zero. |

### Empty versus unavailable results
| Situation | Response |
| --- | --- |

The API confirms the county exists in the current release. It returns HTTP 200 with `availability` set to `UNAVAILABLE`, `reason` set to `CANONICAL_GEOGRAPHY_UNPUBLISHED`, and `data` set to `null`. | --- | --- |
| `400` | The ID is malformed, or you asked for a state. Send a five-digit county FIPS code. |
| `404` | The county is not in the current release. |
| `503` | The county directory is unavailable, empty, duplicated, or inconsistent with the current release. Retry later. |

The response must not be cached.

query.description: Limit rows to one state. Use a two-letter uppercase USPS state code, or `ALL` for every state. The default is `ALL`. Any other value returns 422.

Filter rows by text. Matching ignores case and keeps rows where the county name, state code, or county FIPS code contains the text. Use up to 100 characters; a longer value returns 422. The default is empty, which keeps every row.

Limit rows by available evidence. `all` keeps every county. `ecological` keeps counties with a tick or pathogen signal. `human` keeps counties with a published human case count. `complete` keeps counties whose `evidence_completeness` is 5 or more. The default is `all`. Any other value returns 422.

Percent of the gap score weighted to ecological evidence (tick and pathogen signals). The rest goes to community vulnerability (social vulnerability, insurance access, and rurality). Use a multiple of 5 from 40 to 85. The default is 65. The published score always uses the default. Another value gives a what-if scenario, not the published score. A value outside the accepted range returns 422.

Smoothing constant for the human-case signal. It sets the reported incidence at which the human weakness signal falls to 50: a larger value keeps the signal high for more counties. Use a whole number from 5 to 200. The default is 50. The published score always uses the default. Another value gives a what-if scenario, not the published score. A value outside the accepted range returns 422.

Human weakness signal (0-100) that Atlas assumes for a county with no published human case count or incidence. A missing count is not zero. Use a multiple of 5 from 40 to 90. The default is 75. The published score always uses the default. Another value gives a what-if scenario, not the published score. A value outside the accepted range returns 422.

### Templates
| `template` | What it returns |
| --- | --- |
| `county-v3` (default) | The two-page County Data Brief for the published gap score and Explorer follow-up. It ignores score-setting overrides, so a What-if request cannot change the published score, response category, recommendations, or questions. |
| `county-v1` | The immutable earlier county report. It still binds score settings. |
| `county-v2` | An opt-in report for selected observations. It reads canonical evidence, lineage, value states, and limitations. |

### Key parameters
| Parameter | What to send |
| --- | --- |
| `dataset_version` | Optional release to report on. `county-v2` requires it. |

`ETag` and `If-None-Match` support 304. Published briefs can be cached for 300 seconds with revalidation. `county-v2` responses must not be cached, and the API revalidates authoritative context before it answers 304.

| Response | Cause and what to do |
| --- | --- |
| `404` | A `county-v2` observation is unknown. |
| `413` | The report exceeds the resource limits. Narrow the selection. |
| `422` | The template is unknown, or observation selectors were sent to `county-v1` or `county-v3`. |
| `503` | `county-v2` provenance is missing or mismatched, or the renderer failed or timed out. Retry later. |

- This is surveillance review priority, not Lyme disease risk, predicted incidence, probability, clinical risk, or diagnosis.

info.name: One Health Lyme Gap Atlas API

description.content:
Read-only JSON API for county and state Lyme disease surveillance,
public-health context, and the sources behind them. It is for developers, analysts, and
public-health practitioners. The base URL is
`https://api.onehealthatlas.org`, and public reads need no API key.

## Quickstart
Get the 2023 case-count floor for New York County (FIPS `36061`):

```bash
curl 'https://api.onehealthatlas.org/v1/observations?measure_id=case_count_floor_2023&geography_type=county&geography_id=36061&year=2023'
```

The response is trimmed to the fields that matter. The values are an example:

```json
{
  "data": [{
    "measure_id": "case_count_floor_2023",
    "geography": {"geography_type": "county", "geography_id": "36061"},
    "value": 1114.0, "value_state": "OBSERVED", "unit": "cases",
    "source_label": "CDC Lyme surveillance", "release_id": "...",
    "limitations": ["..."]
  }],
  "meta": {"next_page_token": null, "availability": "AVAILABLE"},
  "links": {"self": null}
}
```

## Responses
Collections return `data` (the items), `meta` (paging, `availability`, `release_id`,
response time), and `links`. A single resource returns `data`.

## Pagination
`page_size` defaults to 100 (maximum 500). Send `meta.next_page_token` as `page_token`,
unchanged and with the same filters. A `null` token means there are no more pages.

## Errors
Errors use RFC 9457 `application/problem+json` with a stable `code` and a `request_id`
to quote when you ask for support. A query that selects more than 10,000 results is
rejected with 400 `QUERY_TOO_BROAD`, not truncated.

## Response headers and caching
Every response has `Content-Type` and `X-Request-ID`; quote the ID when you ask for
support. Each `200` lists its other headers. Cache lifetimes run from 60 seconds to one
year. Detail resources, geometry, and PDF reports return an `ETag`; send it as
`If-None-Match` to get an empty `304`. Other operations always return the full body.

## Rate limits and retries
Metadata, provenance, observation, and geography availability reads are limited per client
address to 60 requests a minute and 5 at once. Other operations have a separate, higher
limit. These defaults can change, and Atlas publishes no per-key quota. A `429` or `503`
can carry `Retry-After` in seconds; wait that long. Without it, wait 1 second, double
after each failure up to 60 seconds, add jitter, and stop after a few attempts. Do not
retry a `400`, `404`, or `422`.

## Interpreting results
Read each value with its `value_state`, source, methodology version, `release_id`, and
`limitations`. Atlas results are not a diagnosis. Atlas results are not an estimate of
an individual's risk. Surveillance floors are minimum counts, not complete incidence.
Null, zero, suppressed, and no linked record mean different things. The response time
shows when Atlas built the response. It does not show when the publisher last updated
the data.

## Stability
`/v1` is the contract version, and the application version is separate. Optional fields
may be added within V1. Breaking changes follow a published deprecation plan.
